title: He didn’t just want influence.
paragraphs:
He didn’t just want influence.
He wanted control.

And his name is buried in one of the shortest letters in the Bible—
but his spirit still walks in rooms today.
Diotrephes.

You won’t find miracles tied to him.
No revival.
No breakthrough moment.
Just one chilling line:
“Diotrephes, who loves to be first…” — 3 John 1:9
Let that sit.

Not “called to lead.”
Not “appointed by God.”
He loved to be first.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.
Because this isn’t just his story.
It can be ours.
The dangerous kind of hunger
There’s a hunger that builds the Kingdom.
And there’s a hunger that builds your name.

Diotrephes didn’t start as a villain.
No one wakes up and says, “I’ll oppose God today.”
It’s slower than that.
Subtle.

Respect turns into expectation.
Expectation turns into entitlement.
Entitlement turns into control.
Until one day…

You’re no longer serving God’s house—
you’re guarding your position in it.
What he actually did (and this is where it gets heavy)
Scripture doesn’t exaggerate. It exposes.
Diotrephes:
Rejected apostolic authority (he refused the leadership of the Apostle John)
Spread malicious words—slander dressed in confidence
Refused to welcome fellow believers
And even put people out of the church who dared to do what was right (3 John 1:10)
Let that sink in.

A man inside the church…
blocking the work of Christ.
Not because of doctrine.
Because of ego.
Here’s the open loop:

How do you follow Jesus—
and still fight to be first?
The mirror hits different now
You don’t need a title to carry the same spirit.
It shows up when:
You feel threatened by someone else’s growth
You secretly want recognition more than righteousness
You serve… but get upset when no one notices
You correct others, but resist correction yourself
That’s not leadership.
That’s Diotrephes—wearing modern clothes.
But now—watch the Gospel break in
Because while Diotrephes was grasping for position…
Jesus was kneeling.

The only One worthy of all authority—
chose a towel.
“Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.” — Mark 9:35
Feel the contrast.

Diotrephes exalts himself.
Jesus empties Himself.

Diotrephes controls people.
Jesus washes their feet.

Diotrephes pushes others out.
Jesus invites sinners in.
This is the turning point
Because the Gospel doesn’t just expose pride—
It offers you a way out.
A better way.
Not by climbing higher…
But by surrendering deeper.
The cross is where “being first” dies

At the cross, your need to be seen—dies.
Your addiction to applause—dies.
Your obsession with status—dies.
And in its place?
Something stronger.
Something freer.
Identity in Christ.

You don’t have to compete
when you’re already chosen.

You don’t have to perform
when you’re already accepted.
You don’t have to be first—
because Jesus already secured your place.
Let’s get real for a moment
Some of you are tired…

Not because ministry is hard—
but because you’re carrying something God never asked you to carry:
the burden of being noticed.
And it’s exhausting.

Because no amount of recognition
will ever heal a heart that hasn’t surrendered.
So here’s the question that cuts deep:
Who is first in your heart?
Not your words.
Not your captions.
Not your public prayers.
Your heart.
Because only one throne exists there.

And if Jesus isn’t sitting on it—
something else is.
The invitation
This isn’t condemnation.
This is mercy.
You can lay it down.

The comparison.
The pride.
The silent competition.

You can come back to Jesus—
not as a performer…
but as a servant who is deeply loved.
And when He becomes first again?
Everything else finds its rightful place.

Leadership becomes service.
Influence becomes stewardship.
And your life becomes a reflection—
not of your greatness—
but of His grace.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
